audit.whatIsWrong: The difficulty story ('knife-fight over his E cooldown') was right but had no number, and the whole early/mid/late block was written in first person ('I have only Bramble Smash'), breaking the page's second-person voice.
audit.why: 51.39% over 72 games is a genuine coin-flip decided by one cooldown; the reader needs the length of that window and the page's own voice.
audit.corrected: early, mid and late rewritten in second person with Heroic Swing's 18s rank-1 cooldown stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike story never tied Maokai's step-up to a real timer.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1 against an 18s Heroic Swing — that ordering is why the 2-3 window is his.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d now give both numbers so the commit is keyed to the gap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heroic Swing was described as 'his dash + camera swing escape' with no mechanics, and the packet flags that the page never names a single Akshan ability.
audit.why: Heroic Swing must hook terrain to fire and is knocked off by champion or terrain collision — it is not a free escape in open lane. Comeuppance is a projectile to the first champion hit, and Twisted Advance is untargetable in flight, so the dash rides through it.
audit.corrected: report[5].t, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, early and mid now name Avengerang, Heroic Swing, Going Rogue and Comeuppance and state the terrain/collision behaviour and the untargetable dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns on the page at all.
audit.why: Heroic Swing 18s->12s, Avengerang 9s->5s, Comeuppance 100s, Twisted Advance 14s are the timers this lane runs on.

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Heroic Swing: 18s at rank 1, 12s at rank 5 — it must hook terrain, so mid-lane he cannot swing out. - Avengerang: 9s poke. - Twisted Advance: 14s, spend it inside his swing gap. - Nature's Grasp: 130s, kill windows only.

edits.before: His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Heroic Swing needs terrain to hook — 18s at rank 1. Step up inside that gap, not before.

edits.before: Track Akshan's Heroic Swing: His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. When it is down — W-root + sapling chain.
edits.after: Heroic Swing hooks terrain and breaks on champion collision; Twisted Advance is untargetable in flight, so it rides through Comeuppance.

edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely his — I have only Bramble Smash with no follow-up, so I just farm with the Q tip and accept his Q poke rather than walking into a swing-trade I can't win. The lane flips the moment I complete W+Q at 2-3: if he steps up to Q a minion and his E grapple is on cooldown, I Twisted Advance onto him, Bramble Smash him out of the wave, and proc Sap Magic to heal the poke right back. The whole danger is his E — if it's up he just grapples out of my root range, so I never burn W unless his swing is down.
edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely his — you have only Bramble Smash with no follow-up, so farm with the Q tip and eat his Avengerang poke rather than walking into a swing-trade you can't win. The lane flips the moment W+Q are online at 2-3: if he steps up to Q a minion and Heroic Swing is on cooldown, Twisted Advance onto him, Bramble Smash him out of the wave, and proc Sap Magic to heal the poke right back. The danger is that swing — 18s at rank 1, and while it is up he grapples clear of your root range.

edits.before: Through 4-5 it's a knife-fight over his E cooldown — when it's up he kites and pokes and the lane is his, when it's down I get a free W-Q and Sap Magic erases the trade. At 6 my Nature's Grasp is the equalizer: a long bramble wave that roots him through his grapple, so if he tries to swing across the lane or rotate I can wall him and walk up for the W. I respect his camouflage — he can vanish, reset, and re-engage with a fresh revive passive, so I don't overchase a low Akshan into fog.
edits.after: Through 4-5 it's a knife-fight over Heroic Swing — while it's up he kites and pokes and the lane is his; the seconds it is down buy you a free W-Q and Sap Magic erases the trade. At 6 Nature's Grasp is the equalizer: a long bramble wave that roots him mid-swing, so if he grapples across the lane or rotates, wall him and walk up for the W. Respect Going Rogue — he can vanish, reset and re-engage, so never overchase a low Akshan into fog.

edits.before: This is where I take the lane back. My resists plus constant Sap Magic healing turn his Q/W poke into a rounding error, and he has no scaling burst that punches through a tank, so every time he greeds in for a swing I W-Q lock him for free. He stays a map threat — camouflage roams and grapple picks elsewhere — so I don't sit AFK in lane; I use R to set ganks and convert my lane stability into teamfight CC rather than chasing a kill he'll just revive out of.
edits.after: This is where you take the lane back. Your resists plus constant Sap Magic healing turn Avengerang poke into a rounding error, and he has no scaling burst that punches through a tank, so every time he greeds in for a swing you W-Q lock him for free. He stays a map threat — Going Rogue roams and grapple picks elsewhere — so don't sit AFK in lane; use R to set ganks and convert lane stability into teamfight CC instead of chasing him.

notes: The packet levelChart (Maokai/Akshan/Akshan/Skill/Skill/Akshan/Maokai) disagrees with the page, but the full and content layers already agree with each other and with the prose (level 1 his, 2-3 flips to Maokai, 6 even-to-his, late Maokai), so I did not flip rows on the packet alone. Per the mirror audit, Bramble Smash's derived 'grounding' flag contradicts Riot's description, so no claim that Q denies Heroic Swing. The kit does not state Sapling Toss reveals camouflage, so that claim was left out.
